rules.text: Anyone who swears has to take a sip.
From now on, you can't say the word "drink" or any form of it (like "drinking" or "drinks").
You're no longer allowed to say "I" (except when reading something aloud).
From now on, everyone must drink with their left hand.
An imaginary little goblin is sitting on top of everyone's drink. Before taking a sip, you must lift it off your glass and put it back afterward.
Whenever you're supposed to take a sip, you have to announce it out loud first.
Your glasses have suddenly become so heavy that you have to use both hands whenever you drink.
You're no longer allowed to say "yes" or "no".
Before drinking, you must clink glasses with someone next to you. They don't have to drink too, but they're welcome to.
You have to say "thank you" before taking a sip.
An imaginary flying bug is sitting on your drink. You have to blow it away before taking a sip.
You have to ask for permission before taking a sip.
From now on, you may only drink with your eyes closed.
Whenever you drink, you must touch another player with one hand.
After taking a sip, you have to make a sound of enjoyment (for example, "Mmm, delicious!", "Whoa, that packs a punch!", or "That's the good stuff!").
From now on, you have to sniff your drink before taking a sip.
Anyone who says a number has to take a sip.
From now on, everyone drinks to {player1}. Say something like "To {player1}!" before each sip. This rule applies to {player1}, too.
Anyone who points at someone with their finger has to take a sip.
You're no longer allowed to scratch your nose or touch your face.
Anyone who interrupts someone else has to take a sip (unless they're pointing out a rule violation).
Anyone who says "What?", "Come again?", or something similar to get the last question repeated has to take a sip (unless it was deliberately read too quietly).
You have to get permission from another player before standing up.
After taking a sip, you must apologize to {player1}. If {player1} is the one drinking, {player1} must apologize to {player2} instead.
After taking a sip, you must thank {player1}. If {player1} is the one drinking, {player1} must thank {player2} instead.
After drinking, you must loudly say “Verdict carried out!”.
Anyone asking a question of their own must begin it with “Your Honor” (except when reading aloud).
From now on, address all other players formally as “Sir” or “Madam”. Anyone who addresses another player informally must drink (except when reading aloud).
Anyone who begins a sentence with “So” must drink (except when reading aloud).
Anyone refusing a request from another player must reply with “Motion denied!”.

Anyone who says “in the end” has to take a sip.

Anyone who says “uh” or “um” while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who looks up or to the side while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who starts a sentence and rephrases it halfway through has to take a sip.
Anyone who says “hm” or “hmm” while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who says “hold on” or “wait a second” while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who says “What was that called again?” has to take a sip.
Anyone who says “Where was I?” has to take a sip.
Anyone who says “What was I saying?” has to take a sip.
Anyone who says “Let me think” has to take a sip.
Anyone who pauses for more than three seconds in the middle of a story has to take a sip.
Anyone who noticeably draws out a word while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who furrows their brow while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who tilts their head while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who touches their chin or face while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who scratches their head while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who briefly closes their eyes while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who drums their fingers on the table while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who bites their lower lip while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who stares into the distance while thinking has to take a sip.
Anyone who audibly sighs before continuing a story has to take a sip.
Anyone who gestures with their hands while telling a story has to take a sip.
Anyone who looks directly at someone to gauge their reaction while telling a story has to take a sip.
Anyone who imitates a person or their voice while telling a story has to take a sip.
Anyone who laughs at their own story while telling it has to take a sip.
Anyone who repeats something several times for emphasis has to take a sip.
Anyone who changes their voice for dramatic effect while telling a story has to take a sip.
Anyone who nods while speaking has to take a sip.
Anyone who makes a thinking noise (e.g. “hmm”, “uh”, or “um”) has to take a sip.
